reason: Credit support to AI cloud partners is part of q09's total of financing commitments and backstops to customers and partners, but this question checks the amount by 2027-12-31 (later quarterly filings), while q09 checks it at FY2027 year-end, and a newly launched programme can grow a lot in between.
Both ask whether the Vera Rubin generation starts shipping by 2026-12-31.
Both ask whether China lets Nvidia H200 chips into the country by the end of January 2027; 'permit sales' and 'authorize imports' are two wordings of one decision.
Both ask how much the largest hyperscalers spend on data-center capex in calendar 2027, and the $1 trillion threshold is settled by that same number.
Both ask when Rubin Ultra starts shipping in Kyber racks; the 2028 deadline is a later deadline of the same shipment event, which D248 boundary 2 keeps as one question.

NVIDIA's supply purchase commitments are a separate 10-K total, owed to suppliers, which moves apart from q09's financing and backstops to customers; only the capacity NVIDIA has agreed to absorb touches q09.

The share of Chinese accelerator budgets going to domestic suppliers by mid-2027 is a different measure, over a different period, from NVIDIA's share of China's 2026 accelerator spending, though the two move against each other.

It compares DRAM and NAND prices at the end of 2027 with the end of 2026, while q05 compares server DRAM and HBM over the whole calendar year; NAND against HBM, and year-end against full-year, can give different answers.

Credit support for AI cloud partners' financing is the core part of q09's financing-and-backstop total, checked in the same FY2027 10-K; under D248 boundary 1 a part of a plan already asked by amount is the same question.
Both ask whether Vera Rubin reaches first shipments by the end of 2026.
Both ask whether Beijing lets H200 chips into China by the end of January 2027.
The $1 trillion test is settled by the same number q13 asks for: the four largest hyperscalers' combined data-center capex in calendar 2027.
Whether Kyber NVL144 racks for Rubin Ultra ship in 2027 or slip to 2028 is settled by q18's yes or no for 2027.

The supply purchase commitments (memory, components and capacity, against the reported $119 billion) are a different 10-K total from q09's customer financing and backstops, and an analyst tracks them apart.
It asks whether Rubin Ultra GPUs ship in 2027 in any rack, Oberon or Kyber, so if Kyber slips to 2028 while Rubin Ultra ships in Oberon racks, this answers yes and q18 answers no.
A US law phasing out Chinese lidar touches no reference question.
The domestic suppliers' share of Chinese accelerator budgets by mid-2027 is a different measure and period from NVIDIA's share of China's 2026 accelerator spending.
A US Commerce enforcement action over chips diverted to DeepSeek is a US-side event that no reference question asks about; q08 asks about China's own import authorization.

The credit support and backstops NVIDIA gives AI cloud partners make up q09's financing-and-backstop total, checked in the same FY2027 10-K; under D248 boundary 1 a part merges into the plan's amount question.
Both ask whether Vera Rubin begins shipping to customers in calendar 2026.
Both ask whether China allows H200 sales or imports for Chinese customers by NVIDIA's FY2027 year-end, which is the end of January 2027.
Its main check is the big four's calendar-2026 data-center capex (q04), but it bundles in the 2027 level, which is the separate bet q13.
Its core is the same Kyber NVL144 Rubin Ultra shipment event; the 2028 date is a later deadline (D248 boundary 2), and the NVL576 follow-on is a later milestone of the same generation (boundary 3).
Purchase commitments to the memory, CoWoS and component supply chain are a different 10-K total from q09's financing and backstops to customers, and an analyst watches each on its own.
Broadcom and Marvell's custom-silicon revenue in calendar 2027 is a different year and a different measure from cloud providers' spending on custom ASICs in calendar 2026.
Both ask how HBM and DRAM contract prices in calendar 2027 move against 2026.

It asks whether Rubin Ultra ships in 2027 in the two-chiplet design, in any rack, while q18 asks whether it ships in Kyber NVL144 racks; each has a condition the other lacks, so the answers can differ.
No reference question asks about SambaNova's and Rebellions' 2026 revenue; it is at most distant evidence for NVIDIA's accelerator share (q06).
